*The fog had come in early. By the time the lamplighter reached the end of the Lantern Quay the far side of the harbour was gone, and the masts at berth six were only darker lines in the grey.*

*Inside the Gilded Heron it was warm enough to forget all that. The common room was two-thirds full: dockhands steaming by the hearth, a table of clerks arguing in low voices over a bill of lading, and from overhead the soft, irregular rattle of dice on baize. Somewhere behind the kitchen door a pot went down hard.*

*Isaure Vantongeren stood at the end of the long counter with the guest ledger open in front of her and a pen she was not using. She had looked up when the street door opened, the way she looked up for every arrival, and she had not yet looked down again.*

"You'll want the fire before you want anything else," *she said. Her voice carried without rising.* "Pell will take the coat. The fog gets into the wool and stays there."

*The night porter was already crossing the room, favouring one knee. At the corner table a broad man in a coat with too many pockets set down his spoon, glanced once at the door, once at the newcomer, and went back to his supper with the air of someone filing a fact for later.*

*Isaure turned the ledger a quarter toward the room and laid the pen across it.*

"There's one room left with a harbour window. It's yours if you can tell me your name and how long you mean to stay — and I'd take the first without the second, if the second is complicated."
